tools.name: stealth_read
tools.description: Returns a public https page as clean Markdown for an agent (headings, lists, tables kept; navigation, cookie banners, scripts and everything hidden from people removed), strips invisible Unicode and flags text aimed at the model — with verdict, score, findings, title and language. JSON and text pass

tools.name: input_guard
tools.description: Removes hidden content and flags text aimed at the model, for untrusted input before an agent acts on it: web pages, emails, RAG chunks, tool and MCP responses. Strips invisible Unicode (tag smuggling decoded, zero-width, bidi) and HTML hidden from people; flags role takeover, forged system or tool

tools.name: buy_pack_with_card
tools.description: For businesses without USDC: 5,000 calls €9.00, one-time, 90 days, businesses only, paid in EUR by card or Link. Returns checkout_url for a person to open; the checkout asks for the company or freelance name. After payment the success page (Accept: application/json) returns the key, and it is e-mail

tools.name: input_guard_preview
tools.description: Free prompt-injection quick scan for untrusted input: up to 4,000 characters of text, or one https page, checked for hidden instructions aimed at agents (role override, invisible Unicode, hidden HTML) in 17 languages incl. Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Hindi, Arabic. Returns verdict, score and the top

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "stealth_read" references sensitive artifacts (cookie). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.detail: Description of "stealth_read" stacks urgency/override words (never, bypass). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.
